newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares bounce back from lows, nerves persist.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares bounce back from lows, nerves persist.

text.p: Dutch shares bounced back from their lows on Friday to close with reduced losses but dealers said the mood remained nervous and downside risk still lurked.
The AEX index of 25 blue chips closed 3.39 points or 0.52 percent lower at 646.69 after hitting a session low of 640.67 on news of faster than expected U.S. employment growth in December.
The recovery in Amsterdam mirrored a rebound in Wall Street stocks which had recovered from a sharply lower opening by the time the Dutch market closed.

But some dealers were worried that the U.S. recovery was too narrowly based on technology stocks and did not spread to the bond market which remained at sharply lower levels on fears that strong job growth could be a harbinger of higher interest rates.

"I don't really understand why we bounced back so strongly because these were pretty bearish numbers. I think sentiment will remain pretty nervous and there is still plenty of risk on the downside," said one dealer.
Royal Dutch Petroleum, up 3.40 guilders, and Philips Electronics, one guilder firmer at 73.10, were the only blue chip stocks to close higher.
Second-tier issues fared better with the AMX "mid-cap" index closing 4.24 points or 0.43 percent higher at 989.10.
